_source: Open Source Office - License Scanning Requirements Document
_note: Rule-based policy an OSO admin can edit without touching code. Controls which reject list each risk profile uses, what tier each outcome maps to, and the message shown to developers.
_profiles_comment: Each risk profile picks the reject list that applies to it. 'reject_list' is a key in license-matrix.json (or null for none).

distributed.label: Distributed Software
distributed.description: Shipped to customers as binaries, packages, or source.

server-side.label: Web-based application (server-side backend)
server-side.description: Runs only on Yahoo-operated infrastructure; not conveyed to users.

mobile.label: Mobile app
mobile.description: iOS/Android app shipped through an app store. Distribution rules apply.

internal.label: Internal use only
internal.description: Never leaves Yahoo and is not offered as a network service. Only the banned list blocks.

ai-model.label: OSS AI model
ai-model.description: Model weights/artifacts. Distribution rules apply, plus model-specific terms need OSO review.
ai-model.always_review_reason: OSS AI model licenses (RAIL, Llama Community, Gemma, OpenRAIL-M and similar) carry use restrictions that a license identifier alone does not capture.

_flag_comment: When true, a license that is rejected for a stricter profile but permitted for this repo's profile is reported as yellow rather than green -- e.g. GPL in a server-side repo is fine today but blocks any future distribution. Set false to silence those.
_cloned_comment: Doc: 'Red Cloned repo - do not allow patching of open source software in cloned repo for certain license types (protect against copyleft)'. Forks are detected automatically; add any non-fork clone here.
_tiers_comment: Tier ordering is fixed in code (green < yellow < red < red-cloned). 'blocks_build' drives the exit code together with --fail-on.
_messages_comment: Custom warning text per outcome. {license}, {package}, {version}, {repo}, {profile} are substituted. 'by_license' overrides the generic text for a specific OSO license name or family prefix.

messages.green: {license} is on the OSO approved list. No action needed.
messages.banned: {license} is on the OSO banned list and is not permitted in any Yahoo repository. Remove {package}@{version} or contact the Open Source Office for an exception.
messages.rejected: {license} is not permitted for {profile} code ({package}@{version}). Remove the dependency, replace it, or file an exception with the Open Source Office.
messages.rejected_by_stricter_profile: {license} is permitted for {profile} use but would block distribution. If {repo} may ever ship to customers, contact the Open Source Office before relying on {package}@{version}.
messages.review: {license} is not on the OSO approved or rejected lists. The Open Source Office needs to review this use of {package}@{version}.
messages.unknown: No license could be determined for {package}@{version}. Declare the license or contact the Open Source Office.
messages.cloned: {repo} is a cloned/forked repository containing {license} code ({package}@{version}). Patching copyleft-licensed code in a clone is not permitted without Open Source Office approval.

by_license.AGPL: AGPL obligations extend to users reached over a network, so it is banned for all Yahoo code regardless of how it is deployed. Remove {package}@{version}.
by_license.GPL: GPL is strong copyleft. It may not ship in distributed code. Contact the Open Source Office before using {package}@{version}.
by_license.LGPL: LGPL is weak copyleft: distributing it requires dynamic linking and relink rights. {package}@{version} may not ship in distributed code without Open Source Office approval of the linking model.
by_license.Open Software: The Open Software License has network-use obligations similar to AGPL. Not permitted. Remove {package}@{version}.
by_license.European: EUPL is copyleft with a compatibility clause. The Open Source Office must approve any use of {package}@{version}.

messages.multiple_detected: Several licenses were detected in {package}@{version} ({license}), so the effective license is unclear. The Open Source Office needs to confirm which one governs before this can be treated as approved.

_ignore_comment: Package ecosystems excluded from the scan. GitHub Actions are build tooling: they never ship in an artifact, so they create no distribution obligation, and GitHub's SBOM reports no license for them at all -- leaving them in made every repo with a workflow file yellow. Values are purl types (githubactions, npm, pypi, golang, gem, maven, ...). Ignored packages are counted in every report so the exclusion stays visible.
_dump_comment: An AND chain of this many licenses or more is treated as a scanner dump rather than a real conjunction. GitHub's SBOM joins every license text it found in a package with AND, so django arrives as 'BSD-3-Clause AND Python-2.0 AND GPL-1.0-or-later AND ...' and strictest-wins would call it GPL. Repeated terms and scanner LicenseRefs are always treated as a dump regardless of this number. Raise it to be stricter, set it very high to disable the length test.
_reporting_comment: Doc action item: 'Define reporting requirements (incremental/full/license level/etc)'. The report always contains the full picture; 'incremental' adds a New since last run section by diffing against state/last-run.json.
_jira_comment: Doc: 'Ability auto generate jira tickets when a unapproved licenses are found'. Tickets are only created when --jira is passed; otherwise the intended tickets are written to jira-tickets.json. One ticket per repo per tier, deduplicated via state/jira-index.json.
_fail_comment: Default severity at which the run exits non-zero (exit code 2). Override per run with --fail-on.
